title: Hugh McPherson's Chicago band and first press notice
summary: Going to Chicago in 1936, the McPherson band at the Meadowbrook, and a mention from George Simon.

story.theme_name: Chicago: the jazz migration and its clubs
story.community_name: Going north: working the Chicago jazz scene

blocks.x: school — into going to Duke that fall, which he did. And I also enrolled in Duke that fall. And I stayed there six weeks and left again. But Les graduated from Duke four years later. In the meantime I went back to Chapel Hill, ten miles away, at the University, the campus. And I was playing with Les’ band and also a campus band, and that was the end of my schooling after that. I wound up going to Chicago in 1936 with some fellows that I had met with the Biagini band in Savannah, Georgia, to Tybee Beach, Hank Biagini had a band down there. And I came down to join the band, but I had laid off for three weeks and I had no endurance. So I didn’t get the job. It didn’t make any difference, because I just had laid off three weeks. But I met all those guys. And this was a band that I got — they were the nucleus of a band that was organized in Chicago that fall. That would be 1936. And this guy was from Wheeling, Pennsylvania, and he wound up as a radio announcer, Hugh McPherson was his name. And he organized this band. It was a pretty good band. It was reviewed, we played The Meadowbrook, Frank Dailey’s Meadowbrook. I got an honorable mention write-up by George Simon, and Glenn Miller was with George Simon and they came in there and that was the first time I’d met Glenn. I had heard him before and seen him before. But they heard me play and it was favorable mention.
Your first time that your name showed up in print as far as the music magazine?
